div.head: Ps Cn for 31.1
div.ab: Liberali uero, dum genuscissio eorum facta fuerit coram primario foreste, licebit; aut sine genuscissione, dum remoti sunt a limitibus foreste per decem miliaria; quanto uero propius uenerint, emendet quodlibet miliare uno solido.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 625 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: But for a noble it shall be lawful, provided their knee-cutting has been done before a chief man of the forest; or without knee-cutting, provided they are kept ten miles away from the bounds of the forest; but the nearer they come, let him pay one shilling compensation for every mile.

note.seg: die Einführung der Lähmung der Hunde schreibt Ordric XI (ed. Le Prévost IV 238) Heinrich dem I. zu, wofür auch Galfr. Monm. VII 3 spricht; sie heisst misera Hn 17, besteht vor 1135 laut vieler Quellen, u. a. Blount Tenures ed. Hazlitt 305, wo das Lähmen impediare heisst. Technisch ist später expeditacio (so Henr. II Ass. de for. 14), laut Charta de for. a. 1217, 6 vor 1154 gebräuchlich. Auch private Jagdbesitzer übten sie: Umfravil schenkt 1181 Newminster partem forestæ, ita quod canes pede carebunt; Cart. de Novo-Monast. (Surtees soc.) p. 74. Bischof Hugo von Durham erlaubt: pedes canum eorum non sint truncati; hinter Boldon buke (Surtees soc.) p. xlvi

Ordric XI (ed. Le Prévost IV 238) attributes the introduction of the lawing (lamming) of dogs to Henry I, which Galfr. Monm. VII 3 also supports; it is called misera in Hn 17, and exists before 1135 according to many sources, among others Blount, Tenures, ed. Hazlitt 305, where the laming is called impediare. Later the technical term is expeditacio (so Henr. II Ass. de for. 14), in use before 1154 according to the Charta de for. a. 1217, 6. Private holders of hunting rights practised it too: in 1181 Umfravil gives Newminster partem forestæ, ita quod canes pede carebunt; Cart. de Novo-Monast. (Surtees soc.) p. 74. Bishop Hugh of Durham permits: pedes canum eorum non sint truncati; at the end of Boldon buke (Surtees soc.) p. xlvi
die Lähmung (in uicinio siluarum laut Ordric) geschah im 12. Jh. vor den Förstern, nicht den Forstrichtern
The laming (in uicinio siluarum according to Ordric) took place in the 12th century before the foresters, not the forest judges
